newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut judge sentences rapist Kelly to 16 years.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut judge sentences rapist Kelly to 16 years.

text.p: A Connecticut judge on Thursday sentenced convicted rapist Alex Kelly, who fled the country for eight years to avoid prosecution, to 16 years in jail for a rape committed more than a decade ago.
Kelly, 30, was convicted on June 12 of raping Adrienne Ortolano in Darien, Connecticut, in February 1986, when the two were high school students who had just met at a party.

Stamford Superior Court Judge Kevin Tierney sentenced the former high school wrestling star to the maximum 20 years, suspended after 16 years, meaning Kelly may not have to serve the last four years. He also fined Kelly $10,000.

Outside the courthouse later, Ortolano said, "I'm grateful that Judge Tierney has finally sentenced Alex Kelly appropriately for what he did to me so long ago. I hope this sends a message to other rape victims across the country."

Kelly, who had been free since his conviction on $1 million bond, was taken into custody immediately after the sentencing. The judge rejected Kelly's request to remain free on the same amount of bond pending appeal.
Tierney's decision to allow Kelly free on bond after his conviction was controversial because prosecutors said they feared Kelly would flee the country again.

Kelly fled the United States on the eve of his originally scheduled trial in 1987, and remained an international fugitive until his 1995 surrender in Switzerland. He said he fled because he feared he would not get a fair trial.
Kelly's odyssey took him through 15 countries, including time spent on European ski slopes. Authorities have said his travels were financed by his wealthy parents.

Shortly before sentencing, an emotional Kelly stood and addressed the court and his victim for the first time. "I never meant to hurt her," he said. "I realise now that I did hurt her. I'm sorry. I wish there was something I could do to take the pain away from her."
His victim is now 27, married, and works as a saleswoman for a pharmaceutical company. She went public with her ordeal and her identity after Kelly's conviction.
Kelly faces another trial on charges he raped a second high school student just four days after the rape of Ortolano.
